scope: LIVE on the camera, firmware 5.02.0.V91, model w71c1. fpLossless TEST card (testcard-20260930-g, fpSup.BIN padded to 61,440 B, sha256 cf9f9f78...; AutoRun.txt unchanged 35a3141f...), USB shell + Fast Start 2. FHD 12-bit 29.97 CinemaDNG, SD, static scene, remote MOVON/MOVOFF. Operator authorised the session and the listed memory reads.
headline: a card-installed, non-blocking, same-frame pipeline compressed frames of a live take with the camera's own lossless-JPEG hardware and the camera wrote them as decodable DNGs; the take has no dropped frames. Frame 1 of \CINEMA\A001_250 is 900,096 B against 3,244,544 B stock and decodes with LibRaw.

runs_that_led_here.found: all four hooks armed on the camera; 10 power cycles clean; C03A33C8 called 29 times, never with event 3 -- no take became lossless; the flush hook ran 133 times, all untouched
request log: 0x2D, 0x23, 0x24, 0x2D around one take -- the movie button sends 0x23 (start) and 0x24 (stop), not 3
0x23 admitted: producer facts read on the camera were exact (1936x1090, 12-bit, raster 3,165,372, 30000/1001); RAW workspace reserved and released; but all 133 frames refused
every refusal was the descriptor check: word 15 of each frame's copy is that frame's own buffer address (0x54136800), 0 in the LiveViewState object -- only width, height and format are compared now

question_1_answered.what: does a frame's own allocation cover the 1 KiB-rounded length the engine is told?
question_1_answered.answer: no, by exactly 512 B at FHD 12-bit. frame+0x6C reads 0x31A200 = 3,252,736 B, which is exactly the native request 0x15400 + align512(3,165,372); the allocator grants no slack. The engine is told 3,166,208 B from +0x15400. Every compressed frame here went through the copy fallback.

the_take.timecodes: frame 1 08:32:18:16, frame 94 08:32:21:19: 93 steps for 93 files -- none dropped. The take is shorter than the 5 s between pulses because the start took effect late; the USB shell timed out at +1.5 s.

frame_1.against_frame_2_stock: min 262 max 684 mean 395.01; |diff| mean 0.97, max 8, 99.9th pct 5: sensor noise between two frames of a static scene; the last three rows agree

what_this_is_not: bit-exact proof: frame 1's own original was overwritten by design. The engine's bitstream was proven lossless against a surviving copy on 2026-09-23; here only decodability and noise-level agreement with the neighbour are shown.

fast: one frame in about six was compressed. The copy fallback moves 3 MB word by word through the uncached alias, and the copy-back 0.8 MB the same way, both on the movie task; the shell timed out and the stop took about 10 s.
complete: 13 frames were turned away because all 16 promise slots were waiting for their flush, which the SD aggregation batches.
next: bulk copies instead of volatile word loops (or read in place: the 512 B lies up to the next 1 KiB boundary, and the allocator places these blocks 1 KiB aligned -- an operator decision)
more promise slots than a 64 MiB aggregation batch holds compressed frames
